articles.title: Lean Certifies Claude's Riemann Proof. The Hype Check Follows.
articles.excerpt: Two things arrived in the Chinese AI channels on November 23: a machine-checked proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, and a crowd arguing about what it actually means. ▸ Lean and Mathlib signed off on the…
articles.body: Two things arrived in the Chinese AI channels on November 23: a machine-checked proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, and a crowd arguing about what it actually means. ▸ Lean and Mathlib signed off on the proof. On November 21 the two communities issued a joint statement confirming that Levent Alpöge's Lean library — 17 million lines, 175,187 modules compiled against Mathlib 4.33.1 — states and proves the Riemann Hypothesis. The checks covered four points: definitions correct, code compiles, the theorem is the standard RH rather than a swapped definition, and the export passes independent kernels (lean4lean, the Rust kernel Nanoda, con-leche). The axiom audit found only propext , Classical.choice and Quot.sound (source: @aigc1024 ) . ▸ What the certificate does not settle.

articles.title: Convert a PDF to Markdown with MinerU from the command line
articles.excerpt: You have a PDF report and want it as Markdown: for your notes, or to give to an AI. How do you do it? You copy and paste from the PDF viewer. The headings turn into plain lines, and the tables turn in…
articles.body: You have a PDF report and want it as Markdown: for your notes, or to give to an AI. How do you do it? You copy and paste from the PDF viewer. The headings turn into plain lines, and the tables turn into rows of numbers with no columns. You ask an AI, and it points you to MinerU , which reads the layout and keeps headings and tables. You install it, start its server, and find the command: mineru parse report.pdf --tier standard --pages 1-10 -o report.md --wait 600 Every flag matters. Leave out --pages and you only get the first 10 pages. Leave out --wait and a long document stops waiting after 60 seconds. --tier trades speed for quality. You save it somewhere: a Markdown note, or a pdf2md.sh file.

articles.title: What did the Soviet Union's final deep space probe actually see on Mars?
articles.excerpt: Conspiracy theories surround the odd-looking appearance of a shadow seen in the final images captured by Phobos 2, the Soviet Union’s last mission into deep space.
articles.body: On July 12, 1988, Phobos 2 — one of the Soviet Union's final major planetary exploration probes — was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome aboard a Proton rocket. The spacecraft's mission included the study of Mars and the Martian moon Phobos, with a planned close approach and deployment of landing probes, and over the next several months, the spacecraft successfully captured more than three dozen images of Phobos during its time in service. However, early in the following year, the spacecraft's mission abruptly ended after the Phobos 2 ground team mysteriously lost contact with the spacecraft.

articles.excerpt: Three stars, 28 light-years, and one big cosmic mystery.
articles.body: A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system. "We were actually looking for planets ," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement . "Instead, we found something much more surprising." So surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years . Furthermore, the configuration of the system seems impossible. "This system should not exist," added Montreal's Patrick Dufour.

articles.title: Robbing Banks is a Blast, But I Wish There Were More Houses to Repair in GTA 6
articles.excerpt: Forget sticking things up with a shotgun, I want to fix things up with a nailgun.
articles.body: My first weekend with Grand Theft Auto 6 was truly mindblowing. The first 20 or so hours I’ve spent with Rockstar’s triumphant return to Vice City have transported me to an impossibly high fidelity game world and treated me to criminal capers so immaculately crafted they make Michael Mann seem more like a Michael mouse. As I’ve made my way across the sprawling Leonida map I’ve relished each and every unethical exploit of lawbreaking lovebirds, Jason and Lucia. So far I’ve been Jason the wheelman, Jason the bagman, and Jason the hitman, but to my surprise, what I really want to be is… Tim the Toolman? Before you hit me with one of Tim Allen’s trademark quizzical caveman grunts, let me back up for a moment.
